Package org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr

Class NumberScalar

java.lang.Object
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.Scalar
org.rapidcow.trivnote.libexpr.NumberScalar
All Implemented Interfaces:
Atom, Datum
public abstract sealed class NumberScalar extends Scalar
Numeric scalar. The scalar is stored and compared symbolically, without regards to the numeric value.

Use Scalar.ofNumber(String) to parse and construct a numeric scalar.

The syntax is mostly based on Racket’s grammar. There are four orthogonally represented components:

  • Prefix: This is an optional component that specifies the radix (#b = 2, #o = 8, #d = 10, #x = 16), or the exactness (#i = inexact, #e = exact), or both. An unspecified radix is equivalent to 10. Note that while the radix applies to both the significand and the exponent in Racket, it only applies to the significand for us.
  • Sign: Optional; positive (+) or negative (-).
  • Significand: Required. This is also the only field subject to radix specification in the prefix under our model. The significand may be in fixed point notation (like 5, 3.14). A notable deviation from R7RS is that digits may terminate in # to indicate uncertainty, though it must occur at the end (e.g., no 12#.4#) and at least some numbers must come before it (e.g., no .##1). It may also be in fraction notation, in which case the numerator and denominator are unsigned integers separated by /. Because of how the way this is spelled is awfully similar to sign, it is given as mantissa in the method name here.
  • Exponent: Optional powers of 10 exponent of the form e+N or powers of 2 of the form p+N; with the exponent letter included. The exponent itself is in radix 10 (decimal), irrespective of the radix specified by the prefix.

The following identities should hold true:

  • value().equals( prefix() + number() );
  • number().equals( sign() + mantissa() + exponent() );
Since:
0.1.0
